subs.title: Tangents, Normals and Rate of Change
Monotonicity, Rolle's and Mean Value Theorems

questions.q: The value of the definite integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(1+e^{-x^2})dx\) is
questions.sol: On \((0,1)\): \(e^{-1}<e^{-x^2}<1\), so the integral lies strictly between \(1+e^{-1}\) and \(2\).

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) be non zero real numbers such that \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(1+\cos^8x)(ax^2+bx+c)dx=\int_0^2(1+\cos^8x)(ax^2+bx+c)dx\). Then the quadratic equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) has
questions.sol: Subtracting: \(\displaystyle\int_1^2(1+\cos^8x)(ax^2+bx+c)dx=0\) with \(1+\cos^8x>0\), so the quadratic must change sign in \((1,2)\).

questions.q: The area bounded by the curves \(y=f(x)\), the \(x\)-axis and the ordinates \(x=1\) and \(x=b\) is \((b-1)\sin(3b+4)\). Then \(f(x)\) is
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int_1^bf(x)dx=(b-1)\sin(3b+4)\); differentiate with respect to \(b\).

questions.q: \(AB\) is a diameter of a circle and \(C\) is any point on the circumference of the circle. Then
opts: the area of \(\Delta ABC\) is maximum when it is isosceles
the area of \(\Delta ABC\) is minimum when it is isosceles
the perimeter of \(\Delta ABC\) is minimum when it is isosceles
questions.sol: The area is \(\frac12AB\times\)(height of \(C\) above \(AB\)), greatest when \(C\) is at the top of the semicircle, i.e. \(CA=CB\).

questions.q: If \(y=a\ln x+bx^2+x\) has its extremum values at \(x=-1\) and \(x=2\), then
questions.sol: \(y'=\dfrac ax+2bx+1\) vanishes at \(-1\) and \(2\): \(-a-2b+1=0\) and \(\dfrac a2+4b+1=0\), giving \(b=-\dfrac12\), \(a=2\).

questions.q: Let \(p(x)=a_0+a_1x^2+a_2x^4+\ldots+a_nx^{2n}\) be a polynomial in a real variable \(x\) with \(0<a_0<a_1<a_2<\ldots<a_n\). The function \(p(x)\) has
opts: Only one maximum and only one minimum
questions.sol: \(p'(x)=x\left(2a_1+4a_2x^2+\ldots+2na_nx^{2n-2}\right)\) and the bracket is positive, so \(p'\) changes sign only at \(x=0\), from negative to positive.

questions.q: The smallest positive root of the equation, \(\tan x-x=0\) lies in
questions.sol: On \(\left(0,\frac\pi2\right)\), \(\tan x>x\); on \(\left(\frac\pi2,\pi\right)\), \(\tan x<0<x\). On \(\left(\pi,\frac{3\pi}2\right)\), \(\tan x-x\) goes from \(-\pi\) to \(+\infty\), so it has a root.

questions.q: Let \(f\) and \(g\) be increasing and decreasing functions, respectively from \([0,\infty)\) to \([0,\infty)\). Let \(h(x)=f(g(x))\). If \(h(0)=0\), then \(h(x)-h(1)\) is
questions.sol: \(h\) is decreasing (increasing of decreasing) and \(h\ge0\). So \(0\le h(x)\le h(0)=0\) for all \(x\ge0\): \(h\equiv0\).

questions.q: Which one of the following curves cut the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) at right angles ?
questions.sol: The parabola has slope \(\dfrac{2a}y\). For \(y=e^{-x/2a}\) the slope is \(-\dfrac y{2a}\), and the product is \(-1\) at every common point. (\(x^2=4ay\) meets the parabola also at \((4a,4a)\), where the slopes are \(2\) and \(\frac12\).) (The book key prints (d).)

questions.q: The function defined by \(f(x)=(x+2)e^{-x}\) is
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=-(x+1)e^{-x}\): positive for \(x<-1\), negative for \(x>-1\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\dfrac{\ln(\pi+x)}{\ln(e+x)}\) is
questions.sol: \(f'\) has the sign of \((e+x)\ln(e+x)-(\pi+x)\ln(\pi+x)\), which is negative because \(t\ln t\) is increasing for \(t>1\) and \(e<\pi\).

questions.q: On the interval \([0,1]\) the function \(x^{25}(1-x)^{75}\) takes its maximum value at the point
questions.sol: \(f'=x^{24}(1-x)^{74}\left[25(1-x)-75x\right]=0\) at \(x=\dfrac14\), where \(f'\) changes from \(+\) to \(-\).

questions.q: The slope of the tangent to a curve \(y=f(x)\) at \([x,f(x)]\) is \(2x+1\). If the curve passes through the point \((1,2)\), then the area bounded by the curve, the \(x\)-axis and the line \(x=1\) is
questions.sol: \(y=x^2+x+c\) through \((1,2)\): \(c=0\). The curve meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x=0\) (and \(-1\)): \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(x^2+x)dx=\dfrac13+\dfrac12\).

questions.q: Let \(P(a\sec\theta,b\tan\theta)\) and \(Q(a\sec\phi,b\tan\phi)\), where \(\theta+\phi=\dfrac\pi2\), be two points on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). If \((h,k)\) is the point of intersection of the normals at \(P\) and \(Q\) then \(k\) is equal to
questions.sol: Normals: \(ax\cos\theta+by\cot\theta=a^2+b^2\) and (with \(\phi=\frac\pi2-\theta\)) \(ax\sin\theta+by\tan\theta=a^2+b^2\). Multiplying by \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\) and subtracting: \(by(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)=(a^2+b^2)(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\sin^4x+\cos^4x\) increases if
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=4\sin x\cos x(\sin^2x-\cos^2x)=-\sin4x>0\) when \(\pi<4x<2\pi\), i.e. \(\dfrac\pi4<x<\dfrac\pi2\).

questions.q: If the normal to the curve \(y=f(x)\) at the point \((3,4)\) makes an angle \(3\pi/4\) with the positive \(x\)-axis, then \(f'(3)=\)
questions.sol: The normal has slope \(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}4=-1\), so the tangent has slope \(1\).

questions.q:
Consider the following \(S\) and \(R\).
\(S\) : Both \(\sin x\), \(\cos x\) are decreasing functions in the interval \(\left(\dfrac\pi2,\pi\right)\)
\(R\) : If a differentiable function decreases in an interval \((a,b)\) then its derivative also decreases in \((a,b)\)
Which of the following is true?
opts: Both \(S\) and \(R\) are correct, but \(R\) is not the correct explanation for \(S\).
\(S\) is correct and \(R\) is the correct explanation for \(S\).
questions.sol: \(S\) is true. \(R\) is false: \(\sin x\) decreases on \(\left(\frac\pi2,\pi\right)\) and so does its derivative \(\cos x\), but \(\cos x\) also decreases there while its derivative \(-\sin x\) increases.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}|x|;&\text{for }0<|x|\le2\\1;&\text{for }x=0\end{cases}\), then at \(x=0\), \(f\) has
The triangle formed by the tangent to the curve \(f(x)=x^2+bx-b\) at the point \((1,1)\) and the coordinate axes, lies in the first quadrant if its area is \(2\), then the value of \(b\) is
questions.sol: Tangent: \(y-1=(2+b)(x-1)\), with intercepts \(\dfrac{1+b}{2+b}\) and \(-(1+b)\). Area: \(-\dfrac{(1+b)^2}{2(2+b)}=2\) gives \((b+3)^2=0\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=xe^{x(1-x)}\), then \(f(x)\) is
The points on the curve \(y^3+3x^2=12y\) where the tangent is vertical, is (are)
Let \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_1^x\sqrt{2-t^2}\,dt\), then the real roots of the equation \(x^2-f'(x)=0\) are
The area bounded by the curves \(y=|x|-1\) and \(y=-|x|+1\) is
questions.sol: The curves enclose the square with vertices \((\pm1,0)\), \((0,\pm1)\), whose diagonals are \(2\): area \(\frac12\cdot2\cdot2\).

questions.q: In \([0,1]\), Lagrange's Mean Value theorem is not applicable to
questions.sol: In (a) the left and right derivatives at \(x=\frac12\) are \(-1\) and \(0\): not differentiable inside \((0,1)\). The others are differentiable on \((0,1)\) and continuous on \([0,1]\).

questions.q: Tangent is drawn to ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{27}+y^2=1\) at \(\left(3\sqrt3\cos\theta,\sin\theta\right)\) (where \(\theta\in(0,\pi/2)\)). Then the value of \(\theta\) such that sum of intercepts on axes made by this tangent is minimum, is
questions.sol: Intercepts: \(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{\cos\theta}\) and \(\dfrac1{\sin\theta}\). Setting the derivative of the sum to zero: \(\tan^3\theta=\dfrac1{3\sqrt3}\), \(\tan\theta=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: The area bounded by the curves \(y=\sqrt x\), \(2y+3=x\) and \(x\)-axis in the \(1^{st}\) quadrant is
questions.sol: They meet where \(y^2=2y+3\), \(y=3\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^3\left[(2y+3)-y^2\right]dy=9+9-9\).

questions.q: The area enclosed between the curves \(y=ax^2\) and \(x=ay^2\) \((a>0)\) is \(1\) sq. unit, then the value of \(a\) is
questions.sol: The curves meet at \((0,0)\) and \(\left(\frac1a,\frac1a\right)\); the area is \(\displaystyle\int_0^{1/a}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac xa}-ax^2\right)dx=\dfrac1{3a^2}=1\).

questions.q: The area bounded by the angle bisectors of the lines \(x^2-y^2+2y=1\) and the line \(x+y=3\), is
questions.sol: \(x^2-(y-1)^2=0\) is the pair \(y-1=\pm x\) through \((0,1)\), whose bisectors are \(x=0\) and \(y=1\). With \(x+y=3\) they form the triangle \((0,1),(0,3),(2,1)\) of area \(\frac12\cdot2\cdot2\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)\) is differentiable and strictly increasing function, then the value of \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{f(x^2)-f(x)}{f(x)-f(0)}\) is
questions.sol: By L'Hôpital's rule: \(\dfrac{2xf'(x^2)-f'(x)}{f'(x)}\to\dfrac{0-f'(0)}{f'(0)}\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=x^\alpha\log x\) and \(f(0)=0\), then the value of \(\alpha\) for which Rolle's theorem can be applied in \([0,1]\) is
questions.sol: Continuity at \(0\) needs \(x^\alpha\log x\to0\), i.e. \(\alpha>0\); then \(f(0)=f(1)=0\) and \(f\) is differentiable on \((0,1)\).

questions.q: If \(P(x)\) is a polynomial of degree less than or equal to \(2\) and \(S\) is the set of all such polynomials so that \(P(0)=0\), \(P(1)=1\) and \(P'(x)>0\ \forall\ x\in[0,1]\), then
questions.sol: \(P=ax+(1-a)x^2\) satisfies the two values. \(P'=a+2(1-a)x\) is linear, so it is positive on \([0,1]\) iff \(P'(0)=a>0\) and \(P'(1)=2-a>0\).

questions.q: Minimum area of the triangle formed by any tangent to the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) with the coordinate axes is
questions.sol: The tangent at \((a\cos\theta,b\sin\theta)\) has intercepts \(\dfrac a{\cos\theta},\dfrac b{\sin\theta}\): area \(\dfrac{ab}{\sin2\theta}\ge ab\).

questions.q: The area bounded by the curve \(y=(x+1)^2\), \(y=(x-1)^2\) and the line \(y=\dfrac14\) is
questions.sol: The parabolas meet at \((0,1)\) and cut \(y=\frac14\) at \(x=\mp\frac12\). Area \(=2\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}\left[(x-1)^2-\dfrac14\right]dx=2\left[\dfrac{(x-1)^3}3-\dfrac x4\right]_0^{1/2}=2\cdot\dfrac16\).

questions.q: The total number of local maxima and local minima of the function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}(2+x)^3,&-3<x\le-1\\x^{2/3},&-1<x<2\end{cases}\), is
questions.sol: \(f\) increases on \((-3,-1]\), decreases on \((-1,0)\) and increases on \((0,2)\) (it is continuous at \(-1\)): a local maximum at \(x=-1\) and a local minimum at \(x=0\).

questions.q: The area of the region between the curves \(y=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}}\) and \(y=\sqrt{\dfrac{1-\sin x}{\cos x}}\) bounded by the lines \(x=0\) and \(x=\dfrac\pi4\) is
questions.sol: With \(t=\tan\frac x2\): \(1\pm\sin x=\dfrac{(1\pm t)^2}{1+t^2}\), \(\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}\), so the difference of the curves is \(\dfrac{2t}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\) and \(dx=\dfrac{2\,dt}{1+t^2}\); the upper limit is \(\tan\frac\pi8=\sqrt2-1\).

questions.q: Let the function \(g:(-\infty,\infty)\to\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) be given by \(g(u)=2\tan^{-1}(e^u)-\dfrac\pi2\). Then, \(g\) is
opts: even and is strictly increasing in \((0,\infty)\)
odd and is strictly decreasing in \((-\infty,\infty)\)
odd and is strictly increasing in \((-\infty,\infty)\)
neither even nor odd, but is strictly increasing in \((-\infty,\infty)\)
questions.sol: \(g(-u)=2\left(\dfrac\pi2-\tan^{-1}e^u\right)-\dfrac\pi2=-g(u)\), and \(g'(u)=\dfrac{2e^u}{1+e^{2u}}>0\).

questions.q: Let \(f,g\) and \(h\) be real-valued functions defined on the interval \([0,1]\) by \(f(x)=e^{x^2}+e^{-x^2}\), \(g(x)=xe^{x^2}+e^{-x^2}\) and \(h(x)=x^2e^{x^2}+e^{-x^2}\). If \(a,b\) and \(c\) denote, respectively, the absolute maximum of \(f,g\) and \(h\) on \([0,1]\), then
questions.sol: On \([0,1]\): \(h\le g\le f\) (as \(x^2\le x\le1\)), \(f\) is increasing, and all three equal \(e+\dfrac1e\) at \(x=1\). So each maximum is \(e+\dfrac1e\).

Let \(f:[-1,2]\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous function such that \(f(x)=f(1-x)\) for all \(x\in[-1,2]\). Let \(R_1=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^2xf(x)dx\), and \(R_2\) be the area of the region bounded by \(y=f(x)\), \(x=-1\), \(x=2\), and the \(x\)-axis. Then
questions.sol: Replacing \(x\) by \(1-x\): \(R_1=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^2(1-x)f(x)dx=R_2-R_1\).

questions.q: Let \(f:\left[\dfrac12,1\right]\to R\) (the set of all real numbers) be a positive, non-constant and differentiable function such that \(f'(x)<2f(x)\) and \(f\left(\dfrac12\right)=1\). Then the value of \(\displaystyle\int_{1/2}^1f(x)dx\) lies in the interval
questions.sol: \(\left(e^{-2x}f\right)'<0\), so \(e^{-2x}f(x)<e^{-1}f\left(\frac12\right)\), i.e. \(f(x)<e^{2x-1}\). Hence \(0<\displaystyle\int_{1/2}^1f<\int_{1/2}^1e^{2x-1}dx=\dfrac{e-1}2\).

questions.q: The number of points in \((-\infty,\infty)\), for which \(x^2-x\sin x-\cos x=0\), is
questions.sol: \(f(x)=x^2-x\sin x-\cos x\) is even, \(f(0)=-1\) and \(f'(x)=x(2-\cos x)>0\) for \(x>0\) with \(f\to\infty\): one positive root and, by symmetry, one negative root.

questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves \(y=\sin x+\cos x\) and \(y=|\cos x-\sin x|\) over the interval \(\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right]\) is
questions.sol: The difference is \(2\sin x\) on \(\left[0,\frac\pi4\right]\) and \(2\cos x\) on \(\left[\frac\pi4,\frac\pi2\right]\): area \(2\left(1-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)\cdot2=4-2\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The least value of \(a\in R\) for which \(4ax^2+\dfrac1x\ge1\), for all \(x>0\), is
questions.sol: AM–GM: \(4ax^2+\dfrac1{2x}+\dfrac1{2x}\ge3(a)^{1/3}\). So the minimum is \(3a^{1/3}\ge1\), i.e. \(a\ge\dfrac1{27}\).

questions.q: Area of the region \(\left\{(x,y)\in R^2:y\ge\sqrt{|x+3|},\ 5y\le x+9\le15\right\}\) is equal to
questions.sol: The line \(5y=x+9\) meets \(y=\sqrt{|x+3|}\) at \((-4,1)\) and \((1,2)\) (and touches the region's limit at \(x=6\)). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_{-4}^1\dfrac{x+9}5dx-\int_{-4}^{-3}\sqrt{-x-3}\,dx-\int_{-3}^1\sqrt{x+3}\,dx=\dfrac{15}2-\dfrac23-\dfrac{16}3\).

questions.q: If \(f:R\to R\) is a twice differentiable function such that \(f''(x)>0\) for all \(x\in R\), and \(f\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac12\), \(f(1)=1\), then
questions.sol: By the mean value theorem \(f'(c)=\dfrac{1-\frac12}{1-\frac12}=1\) for some \(c\in\left(\frac12,1\right)\), and \(f'\) is increasing, so \(f'(1)>1\).

questions.q: The area of the region \(\{(x,y):xy\le8,\ 1\le y\le x^2\}\) is
questions.sol: \(y=x^2\) and \(xy=8\) meet at \((2,4)\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_1^2(x^2-1)dx+\int_2^8\left(\dfrac8x-1\right)dx=\dfrac43+16\ln2-6\).

questions.q: Let the functions \(f:R\to R\) and \(g:R\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=e^{x-1}-e^{-|x-1|}\) and \(g(x)=\dfrac12\left(e^{x-1}+e^{1-x}\right)\). Then the area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by the curves \(y=f(x)\), \(y=g(x)\) and \(x=0\) is
questions.sol: \(f=0\) for \(x\le1\) and \(e^{x-1}-e^{1-x}\) for \(x\ge1\); \(f=g\) where \(e^{2(x-1)}=3\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^1g\,dx+\int_1^{1+\frac12\ln3}(g-f)dx=\dfrac12(e-e^{-1})+\left[-\dfrac12e^{x-1}-\dfrac32e^{1-x}\right]_1^{1+\frac12\ln3}=\dfrac12(e-e^{-1})+2-\sqrt3\).

questions.q: Consider all rectangles lying in the region \(\left\{(x,y)\in R\times R:0\le x\le\dfrac\pi2\text{ and }0\le y\le2\sin(2x)\right\}\) and having one side on the \(x\)-axis. The area of the rectangle which has the maximum perimeter among all such rectangles, is
questions.sol: By symmetry the rectangle runs from \(x=a\) to \(\frac\pi2-a\) with height \(2\sin2a\). Perimeter \(2\left[\frac\pi2-2a+2\sin2a\right]\) is greatest when \(\cos2a=\frac12\), \(a=\frac\pi6\): width \(\frac\pi6\), height \(\sqrt3\).

questions.q: The area of the region \(\left\{(x,y):0\le x\le\dfrac94,\ 0\le y\le1,\ x\ge3y,\ x+y\ge2\right\}\) is
questions.sol: The region is the quadrilateral with vertices \((2,0)\), \(\left(\frac94,0\right)\), \(\left(\frac94,\frac34\right)\), \(\left(\frac32,\frac12\right)\). Shoelace: \(\dfrac12\left|0+\dfrac{27}{16}+0-1\right|=\dfrac{11}{32}\).

questions.q: Let \(S=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ y^2\le4x,\ y^2\le12-2x\) and \(3y+\sqrt8x\le5\sqrt8\}\). If the area of the region \(S\) is \(\alpha\sqrt2\), then \(\alpha\) is equal to
questions.sol: All three curves pass through \((2,2\sqrt2)\), and for \(0\le y\le2\sqrt2\) the line lies to the left of \(y^2=12-2x\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt2}\left(5-\dfrac{3y}{2\sqrt2}-\dfrac{y^2}4\right)dy=10\sqrt2-3\sqrt2-\dfrac{4\sqrt2}3\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\begin{cases}3x^2+12x-1,&-1\le x\le2\\37-x,&2<x\le3\end{cases}\)
questions.sol: On \([-1,2]\), \(f'=6x+12>0\). At \(2\) both pieces give \(35\); the one-sided derivatives are \(24\) and \(-1\). \(f\) rises to \(35\) at \(x=2\) and then falls, so the maximum is at \(x=2\). (The book prints \(3x^2+12-1\) and its key gives (a), (b), (c); (d) is also true.)

questions.q: Let \(h(x)=f(x)-(f(x))^2+(f(x))^3\) for every real number \(x\), Then
opts: Nothing can be said in general.
questions.sol: \(h'=f'\left(1-2f+3f^2\right)\) and \(3f^2-2f+1>0\) always (negative discriminant), so \(h'\) has the sign of \(f'\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^xt(e^t-1)(t-1)(t-2)^3(t-3)^5dt\) has a local minimum at \(x=\)
For which of the following values of \(m\), is the area of the region bounded by the curve \(y=x-x^2\) and the line \(y=mx\) equals \(9/2\).
questions.sol: They meet at \(x=0\) and \(x=1-m\); the area is \(\left|\displaystyle\int_0^{1-m}\left((1-m)x-x^2\right)dx\right|=\dfrac{|1-m|^3}6=\dfrac92\), so \(1-m=\pm3\).

questions.q: \(f(x)\) is cubic polynomial with \(f(2)=18\) and \(f(1)=-1\). Also \(f(x)\) has local maxima at \(x=-1\) and \(f'(x)\) has local minima at \(x=0\), then
opts: the distance between \((-1,2)\) and \((a,f(a))\), where \(x=a\) is the point of local minima, is \(2\sqrt5\)
questions.sol: \(f''(0)=0\) gives \(f=ax^3+cx+d\); \(f'(-1)=0\) gives \(c=-3a\); \(f(2)=18\), \(f(1)=-1\) give \(a=\dfrac{19}4\), \(d=\dfrac{17}2\). So \(f=\dfrac14(19x^3-57x+34)\), \(f'=\dfrac{57}4(x^2-1)\): local minimum at \(x=1\), increasing for \(x\ge1\). The minimum point is \((1,-1)\), at distance \(\sqrt{13}\) from \((-1,2)\), and \(f(0)=\dfrac{17}2\). (The book prints (c) with \(f'(x)\) and (d) as \(15\); the paper's wording is used.)

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}e^x,&0\le x\le1\\2-e^{x-1},&1<x\le2\\x-e,&2<x\le3\end{cases}\) and \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt\), \(x\in[1,3]\) then \(g(x)\) has
opts: local maxima at \(x=1+\ln2\) and local minima at \(x=e\)
local maxima at \(x=1\) and local minima at \(x=2\)
questions.sol: \(g'=f\). On \((1,2]\), \(f=2-e^{x-1}\) changes from \(+\) to \(-\) at \(x=1+\ln2\): local maximum. On \((2,3]\), \(f=x-e\) changes from \(-\) to \(+\) at \(x=e\): local minimum. Around \(x=2\), \(f\) is negative on both sides, and around \(x=1\) it is positive, so there is no interior extremum there. (The book key prints (a), (b).)

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\) be a non-constant twice differentiable function defined on \((-\infty,\infty)\) such that \(f(x)=f(1-x)\) and \(f'\left(\dfrac14\right)=0\). Then,
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=-f'(1-x)\), so \(f'\) vanishes at \(\frac12\) and at \(\frac34\) as well as \(\frac14\); by Rolle's theorem \(f''\) vanishes twice. \(f\left(x+\frac12\right)\) is even, so (c) has an odd integrand. In (d) put \(t\to1-t\) on the right.

questions.q: For the function \(f(x)=x\cos\dfrac1x\), \(x\ge1\),
opts: for at least one \(x\) in the interval \([1,\infty)\), \(f(x+2)-f(x)<2\)
\(f'(x)\) is strictly decreasing in the interval \([1,\infty)\)
questions.sol: \(f'=\cos\dfrac1x+\dfrac1x\sin\dfrac1x\to1\) and \(f''=-\dfrac1{x^3}\cos\dfrac1x<0\). So \(f'\) decreases to \(1\), hence \(f'>1\), and by the mean value theorem \(f(x+2)-f(x)=2f'(c)>2\).

questions.q: Area of the region bounded by the curve \(y=e^x\) and lines \(x=0\) and \(y=e\) is
questions.sol: The area is \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(e-e^x)dx=1\), which is (c); integrating along \(y\) it is \(\displaystyle\int_1^e\ln y\,dy\) (d), and replacing \(y\) by \(e+1-y\) gives (b).

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a real-valued function defined on the interval \((0,\infty)\) by \(f(x)=\ln x+\displaystyle\int_0^x\sqrt{1+\sin t}\,dt\). Then which of the following statement (s) is (are) true?
opts: \(f'(x)\) exists for all \(x\in(0,\infty)\) and \(f'\) is continuous on \((0,\infty)\), but not differentiable on \((0,\infty)\)
there exists \(\alpha>1\) such that \(|f'(x)|<|f(x)|\) for all \(x\in(\alpha,\infty)\)
there exists \(\beta>0\) such that \(|f(x)|+|f'(x)|\le\beta\) for all \(x\in(0,\infty)\)
questions.sol: \(f'=\dfrac1x+\sqrt{1+\sin x}\) is continuous but \(\sqrt{1+\sin x}=\sqrt2\left|\sin\left(\frac x2+\frac\pi4\right)\right|\) has corners where \(\sin x=-1\). \(f'\) is bounded for \(x>1\) while \(f(x)\to\infty\): (c) true, (d) false.

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the area of the region enclosed by \(y=e^{-x^2}\), \(y=0\), \(x=0\) and \(x=1\). Then
questions.sol: \(e^{-x^2}\ge e^{-x}\) on \([0,1]\) gives \(S\ge1-\dfrac1e\) \((>\frac1e)\). The curve lies under the two rectangles of heights \(1\) (on \(\left[0,\frac1{\sqrt2}\right]\)) and \(e^{-1/2}\) (on \(\left[\frac1{\sqrt2},1\right]\)): (d). \(S\approx0.75\), so (c) fails.

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^xe^{t^2}(t-2)(t-3)dt\) for all \(x\in(0,\infty)\), then
questions.sol: \(f'=e^{x^2}(x-2)(x-3)\): \(+\), \(-\), \(+\) on the three intervals. \(f'(2)=f'(3)=0\), so by Rolle's theorem \(f''(c)=0\) for some \(c\in(2,3)\).

questions.q: A rectangular sheet of fixed perimeter with sides having their lengths in the ratio \(8:15\) is converted into an open rectangular box by folding after removing squares of equal area from all four corners. If the total area of the removed squares is \(100\), the resulting box has maximum volume. The lengths of the sides of the rectangular sheet are
The function \(f(x)=2|x|+|x+2|-||x+2|-2|x||\) has a local minimum or a local maximum at \(x=\)
questions.sol: \(a+b-|a-b|=2\min(a,b)\), so \(f=2\min(2|x|,|x+2|)\). The two graphs cross at \(x=-\frac23\) and \(x=2\). \(f\) falls to \(0\) at \(-2\) (minimum), rises until \(-\frac23\) (maximum), falls to \(0\) at \(0\) (minimum), then keeps rising through \(x=2\).

questions.q: Let \(f:(0,\infty)\to R\) be given by \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_{1/x}^x\dfrac{e^{-\left(t+\frac1t\right)}}tdt\). Then
opts: \(f(2^x)\) is an odd function of \(x\) on \(R\)
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=\dfrac{2e^{-\left(x+\frac1x\right)}}x>0\): increasing everywhere. Interchanging the limits gives \(f\left(\frac1x\right)=-f(x)\), and then \(f(2^{-x})=-f(2^x)\).

questions.q: Let \(f:\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\to R\) be given by \(f(x)=(\log(\sec x+\tan x))^3\). Then
questions.sol: \(\sec(-x)+\tan(-x)=\dfrac1{\sec x+\tan x}\), so \(f\) is odd. \(\sec x+\tan x\) increases from \(0\) to \(\infty\) on the interval, so its logarithm (and its cube) increases from \(-\infty\) to \(\infty\): one-one and onto.

questions.q: Let \(a\in R\) and let \(f:R\to R\) be given by \(f(x)=x^5-5x+a\). Then
opts: \(f(x)\) has only one real root if \(a>4\)
questions.sol: \(f'=5(x^4-1)\): local maximum \(f(-1)=a+4\), local minimum \(f(1)=a-4\). Three real roots iff \(a+4>0>a-4\); otherwise only one.

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to(0,\infty)\) and \(g:R\to R\) be twice differentiable functions such that \(f''\) and \(g''\) are continuous functions on \(R\). Suppose \(f'(2)=g(2)=0\), \(f''(2)\ne0\) and \(g'(2)\ne0\). If \(\lim\limits_{x\to2}\dfrac{f(x)g(x)}{f'(x)g'(x)}=1\), then
questions.sol: By L'Hôpital's rule the limit is \(\dfrac{f'g+fg'}{f''g'+f'g''}\to\dfrac{f(2)g'(2)}{f''(2)g'(2)}=1\), so \(f''(2)=f(2)>0\): a local minimum at \(2\), and \(f-f''=0\) at \(x=2\).

questions.q: If the line \(x=\alpha\) divides the area of region \(R=\{(x,y)\in R^2:x^3\le y\le x,\ 0\le x\le1\}\) into two equal parts, then
questions.sol: Total area \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(x-x^3)dx=\dfrac14\). \(\dfrac{\alpha^2}2-\dfrac{\alpha^4}4=\dfrac18\) gives \(2\alpha^4-4\alpha^2+1=0\), \(\alpha^2=1-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\), \(\alpha\approx0.54\).

questions.q: If \(f:R\to R\) is a differentiable function such that \(f'(x)>2f(x)\) for all \(x\in R\) and \(f(0)=1\), then
If \(f(x)=\begin{vmatrix}\cos2x&\cos2x&\sin2x\\-\cos x&\cos x&-\sin x\\\sin x&\sin x&\cos x\end{vmatrix}\), then
opts: \(f'(x)=0\) at more than three points in \((-\pi,\pi)\)
questions.sol: \(C_1\to C_1-C_2\) gives \(f=2\cos x(\cos2x\cos x-\sin2x\sin x)=2\cos x\cos3x=\cos4x+\cos2x\), with maximum \(2\) at \(x=0\). \(f'=-2\sin2x(4\cos2x+1)=0\) at \(0,\pm\frac\pi2\) and at four more points where \(\cos2x=-\frac14\).

questions.q: For every twice differentiable function \(f:\mathbb R\to[-2,2]\) with \((f(0))^2+(f'(0))^2=85\), which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
opts: There exist \(r,s\in\mathbb R\), where \(r<s\), such that \(f\) is one-one on the open interval \((r,s)\)
questions.sol: \(f(0)^2\le4\) gives \(|f'(0)|\ge9\); \(f'\) keeps its sign near \(0\), so \(f\) is one-one there (a). By the mean value theorem \(|f'(x_0)|=\dfrac{|f(0)-f(-4)|}4\le1\) (b), and similarly at some \(x_1\in(0,4)\). For \(h=f^2+f'^2\): \(h(x_0),h(x_1)\le5\) and \(h(0)=85\), so \(h\) has a maximum at some \(\alpha\in(x_0,x_1)\) with \(h(\alpha)\ge85\): \(h'(\alpha)=2f'(\alpha)\left(f(\alpha)+f''(\alpha)\right)=0\) and \(f'(\alpha)\ne0\) (d). (c) need not hold.

questions.q:
Let \(f:R\to R\) be given by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^5+5x^4+10x^3+10x^2+3x+1,&x<0;\\x^2-x+1,&0\le x<1;\\(2/3)x^3-4x^2+7x-(8/3),&1\le x<3;\\(x-2)\log_e(x-2)-x+(10/3),&x\ge3.\end{cases}\)
Then which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.sol: Near \(1\): \(f'=2x-1\) (left) and \(2x^2-8x+7\) (right), both \(1\) at \(x=1\); \(f''\) is \(2\) and \(-4\): \(f'\) has a corner and a local maximum there. For \(x<0\): \(f'=5(x+1)^4-2<0\) near \(x=-1\). \(f\) is continuous (values \(1,1,\frac13\) match at \(0,1,3\)) with \(f\to\mp\infty\) as \(x\to\mp\infty\): onto.

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be given by \(f(x)=(x-1)(x-2)(x-5)\). Define \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt\), \(x>0\). Then which of the following options is/are correct?
opts: \(F\) has two local maxima and one local minimum in \((0,\infty)\).
questions.sol: \(F'=f\) has signs \(-,+,-,+\): minima at \(1\) and \(5\), maximum at \(2\). \(F(x)=\dfrac{x^4}4-\dfrac{8x^3}3+\dfrac{17x^2}2-10x\), and its largest value on \((0,5)\) is \(F(2)=-\dfrac{10}3<0\), so \(F\ne0\) there.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\dfrac{\sin\pi x}{x^2}\), \(x>0\). Let \(x_1<x_2<x_3<\ldots<x_n<\ldots\) be all points of local maximum of \(f\) and \(y_1<y_2<y_3<\ldots<y_n<\ldots\) be all the points of local minimum of \(f\). Then which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.sol: \(f'=0\) when \(\tan\pi x=\dfrac{\pi x}2\): one root in each \(\left(m,m+\frac12\right)\), \(m\ge1\), at \(m+\frac12-\varepsilon_m\) with \(\varepsilon_m\) decreasing to \(0\). For odd \(m\), \(\sin\pi x<0\) (minimum): \(y_n=2n-\frac12-\varepsilon_{2n-1}\); for even \(m\) (maximum): \(x_n=2n+\frac12-\varepsilon_{2n}\). So \(y_1<x_1\), \(x_n-y_n=1+\varepsilon_{2n-1}-\varepsilon_{2n}>1\) and \(x_{n+1}-x_n=2+\varepsilon_{2n}-\varepsilon_{2n+2}>2\).

questions.q: Let \(b\) be a non-zero real number. Suppose \(f:R\to R\) is a differentiable function such that \(f(0)=1\). If the derivative \(f'\) of \(f\) satisfies the equation \(f'(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{b^2+x^2}\) for all \(x\in R\), then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: If \(b>0\), then \(f\) is an increasing function
If \(b<0\), then \(f\) is a decreasing function
questions.sol: \(f(x)=e^{\frac1b\tan^{-1}\frac xb}>0\), so \(f'>0\) for every \(b\ne0\). The exponent is odd in \(x\), so \(f(x)f(-x)=1\).

questions.q:
Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-3x-6}{x^2+2x+4}\)
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=\dfrac{5x(x+4)}{(x^2+2x+4)^2}\): negative on \((-4,0)\), positive elsewhere. \(f(-4)=\dfrac{11}6\), \(f(0)=-\dfrac32\) and \(f\to1\) at \(\pm\infty\): range \(\left[-\dfrac32,\dfrac{11}6\right]\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha=\sum\limits_{k=1}^\infty\sin^{2k}\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)\). Let \(g:[0,1]\to R\) be the function defined by \(g(x)=2^{\alpha x}+2^{\alpha(1-x)}\). Then, which of the following statements is/are true?
opts: The function \(g(x)\) attains its maximum at more one point
The function \(g(x)\) attains its minimum at more than one point
questions.sol: \(\alpha=\dfrac{1/4}{1-1/4}=\dfrac13\). \(g(x)=2^{x/3}+2^{(1-x)/3}\ge2\sqrt{2^{1/3}}=2^{7/6}\), with equality only at \(x=\dfrac12\). \(g\) is symmetric about \(\frac12\) and convex, so the maximum \(1+2^{1/3}\) is attained at both \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) be the function defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^3}3-x^2+\dfrac59x+\dfrac{17}{36}\). Consider the square region \(S=[0,1]\times[0,1]\). Let \(G=\{(x,y)\in S:y>f(x)\}\) be called the green region and \(R=\{(x,y)\in S:y<f(x)\}\) be called the red region. Let \(L_h=\{(x,h)\in S:x\in[0,1]\}\) be the horizontal line drawn at a height \(h\in[0,1]\). Then which of the following statements is (are) true?
opts: There exists an \(h\in\left[\dfrac14,\dfrac23\right]\) such that the area of the green region above the line \(L_h\) equals the area of the green region below the line \(L_h\)
There exists an \(h\in\left[\dfrac14,\dfrac23\right]\) such that the area of the red region above the line \(L_h\) equals the area of the red region below the line \(L_h\)
There exists an \(h\in\left[\dfrac14,\dfrac23\right]\) such that the area of the green region above the line \(L_h\) equals the area of the red region below the line \(L_h\)
There exists an \(h\in\left[\dfrac14,\dfrac23\right]\) such that the area of the red region above the line \(L_h\) equals the area of the green region below the line \(L_h\)
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int_0^1f=\dfrac12\): red and green areas are both \(\frac12\). On \([0,1]\): \(\min f=f(1)=\dfrac{13}{36}\), \(\max f=f\left(\frac13\right)=\dfrac{181}{324}<\dfrac23\). At \(h=\frac14\) (below the curve): red below \(=\frac14=\) red above — (b) true; green below \(=0\), green above \(=\frac12\). At \(h=\frac23\) (above the curve): green above \(=\frac13\), green below \(=\frac16\), red below \(=\frac12\), red above \(=0\). Green above \(-\) green below stays positive on the interval: (a) false. Green above \(-\) red below changes sign (\(+\frac14\) to \(-\frac16\)): (c) true. Red above \(-\) green below changes sign (\(+\frac14\) to \(-\frac16\)): (d) true.

questions.q: Let \(f:(0,1)\to\mathbb R\) be the function defined as \(f(x)=[4x]\left(x-\dfrac14\right)^2\left(x-\dfrac12\right)\), where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\). Then which of the following statements is(are) true?
opts: The function \(f\) is discontinuous exactly at one point in \((0,1)\)
There is exactly one point in \((0,1)\) at which the function \(f\) is continuous but NOT differentiable
The function \(f\) is NOT differentiable at more than three points in \((0,1)\)
The minimum value of the function \(f\) is \(-\dfrac1{512}\)
questions.sol: With \(p(x)=\left(x-\frac14\right)^2\left(x-\frac12\right)\): \(f=0,\ p,\ 2p,\ 3p\) on the four quarters. At \(\frac14\): \(p\) and \(p'\) vanish — smooth. At \(\frac12\): \(p=0\) but \(p'=\frac1{16}\ne0\) — continuous, not differentiable. At \(\frac34\): \(p=\frac1{16}\ne0\) — discontinuous. On \(\left[\frac14,\frac12\right)\) the minimum of \(p\) is at \(x=\frac5{12}\): \(-\dfrac1{432}\).

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the set of all twice differentiable functions \(f\) from \(\mathbb R\) to \(\mathbb R\) such that \(\dfrac{d^2f}{dx^2}(x)>0\) for all \(x\in(-1,1)\). For \(f\in S\), let \(X_f\) be the number of points \(x\in(-1,1)\) for which \(f(x)=x\). Then which of the following statements is(are) true?
opts: There exists a function \(f\in S\) such that \(X_f=0\)
For every function \(f\in S\), we have \(X_f\le2\)
There exists a function \(f\in S\) such that \(X_f=2\)
There does NOT exist any function \(f\) in \(S\) such that \(X_f=1\)
questions.sol: \(g=f(x)-x\) has \(g''>0\) on \((-1,1)\); three zeros would give two zeros of \(g'\) and then a zero of \(g''\) (Rolle), so \(X_f\le2\). Examples: \(x^2+1\) (\(X_f=0\)), \(2x^2\) (zeros \(0,\frac12\)), \(x^2\) (only \(0\) in the interval).

questions.q: Show that \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(\dfrac1{n+1}+\dfrac1{n+2}+\ldots+\dfrac1{6n}\right)=\log6\).
questions.sol: The sum is \(\dfrac1n\sum\limits_{r=1}^{5n}\dfrac1{1+\frac rn}\to\displaystyle\int_0^5\dfrac{dx}{1+x}=\log6\).

questions.q: Find the area bounded by the curves \(x^2=4y\) and the straight line \(x=4y-2\).
questions.sol: They meet where \(x^2=x+2\): \(x=-1,2\). Area \(=\dfrac14\displaystyle\int_{-1}^2(x+2-x^2)dx=\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac92\).

questions.q: Let \(x\) and \(y\) be two real variables such that \(x>0\) and \(xy=1\). Find the minimum value of \(x+y\).
questions.sol: \(x+\dfrac1x\ge2\) by AM–GM, with equality at \(x=1\).

questions.q: For all \(x\) in \([0,1]\), let the second derivative \(f''(x)\) of a function \(f(x)\) exist and satisfy \(|f''(x)|<1\). If \(f(0)=f(1)\), then show that \(|f'(x)|<1\) for all \(x\) in \([0,1]\).
questions.sol: By Rolle's theorem \(f'(c)=0\) for some \(c\in(0,1)\). For any \(x\), the mean value theorem for \(f'\) gives \(f'(x)=f'(x)-f'(c)=(x-c)f''(d)\), so \(|f'(x)|<|x-c|\le1\).

questions.q: Use the function \(f(x)=x^{1/x}\), \(x>0\), to determine the bigger of the two numbers \(e^\pi\) and \(\pi^e\)
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=x^{1/x}\cdot\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x^2}\): the maximum is at \(x=e\). So \(e^{1/e}>\pi^{1/\pi}\); raising to the power \(e\pi\): \(e^\pi>\pi^e\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) are differentiable function for \(0\le x\le1\) such that \(f(0)=2\), \(g(0)=0\), \(f(1)=6\), \(g(1)=2\), then show that there exist \(c\) satisfying \(0<c<1\) and \(f'(c)=2g'(c)\).
questions.sol: \(h(x)=f(x)-2g(x)\) has \(h(0)=2=h(1)\); by Rolle's theorem \(h'(c)=0\) for some \(c\in(0,1)\).

questions.q: Find the shortest distance of the point \((0,c)\) from the parabola \(y=x^2\) where \(0\le c\le5\).
questions.sol: With \(t=x^2\ge0\): \(D^2=t+(t-c)^2\), minimum at \(t=c-\dfrac12\) when \(c\ge\dfrac12\): \(D^2=c-\dfrac14\). If \(c<\dfrac12\) the minimum is at \(t=0\): \(D=c\).

questions.q: If \(ax^2+\dfrac bx\ge c\) for all positive \(x\) where \(a>0\) and \(b>0\) show that \(27ab^2\ge4c^3\).
questions.sol: \(ax^2+\dfrac b{2x}+\dfrac b{2x}\ge3\left(\dfrac{ab^2}4\right)^{1/3}\), and this minimum is attained; so \(3\left(\dfrac{ab^2}4\right)^{1/3}\ge c\). Cubing: \(27ab^2\ge4c^3\).

questions.q: Show that \(1+x\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)\ge\sqrt{1+x^2}\) for all \(x\ge0\).
questions.sol: Let \(f=1+x\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-\sqrt{1+x^2}\). \(f'=\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+\dfrac x{\sqrt{x^2+1}}-\dfrac x{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\ge0\) for \(x\ge0\), and \(f(0)=0\).

questions.q: Find the area bounded by the \(x\)-axis, part of the curve \(y=1+\dfrac8{x^2}\) and the ordinates at \(x=2\) and \(x=4\). If the ordinate \(x=a\) divides the area into two equal parts find \(a\).
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int_2^4\left(1+\dfrac8{x^2}\right)dx=2+2=4\). \(\displaystyle\int_2^a=(a-2)+4-\dfrac8a=2\) gives \(a^2=8\).

questions.q: A swimmer \(S\) is in the sea at a distance \(d\) km from the closest point \(A\) on a straight shore. The house of the swimmer is on the shore at a distance \(L\) km from \(A\). He can swim at a speed of \(u\) km/hr and walk at a speed of \(v\) km/hr \((v>u)\). At what point on the shore should he land so that he reaches his house in the shortest possible time?
questions.sol: Landing \(x\) km from \(A\): \(T=\dfrac{\sqrt{d^2+x^2}}u+\dfrac{L-x}v\). \(T'=0\) gives \(\dfrac x{\sqrt{d^2+x^2}}=\dfrac uv\), so \(x=\dfrac{ud}{\sqrt{v^2-u^2}}\) (if this exceeds \(L\) he should swim straight to the house).

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the point on the curve \(y=\dfrac x{1+x^2}\) where the tangent to the curve has the greatest slope.
questions.sol: Slope \(m=\dfrac{1-x^2}{(1+x^2)^2}\), \(\dfrac{dm}{dx}=\dfrac{-2x(3-x^2)}{(1+x^2)^3}\): critical points \(0,\pm\sqrt3\). \(m(0)=1\) is the greatest (\(m(\pm\sqrt3)=-\frac18\)), at the point \((0,0)\).

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the \(x\)-axis and the curves defined by \(y=\tan x\), \(-\dfrac\pi3\le x\le\dfrac\pi3\); \(y=\cot x\), \(\dfrac\pi6\le x\le\dfrac\pi2\).
questions.sol: Both curves are available for \(\dfrac\pi6\le x\le\dfrac\pi3\) and they cross at \(x=\dfrac\pi4\). Area under the lower curve: \(\displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}\tan x\,dx+\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3}\cot x\,dx=\ln\dfrac{\sqrt3/2}{1/\sqrt2}+\ln\dfrac{\sqrt3/2}{1/\sqrt2}=\ln\dfrac32\).

questions.q: Find all the tangents to the curve \(y=\cos(x+y)\), \(-2\pi\le x\le2\pi\), that are parallel to the line \(x+2y=0\).
questions.sol: \(y'=-\dfrac{\sin(x+y)}{1+\sin(x+y)}=-\dfrac12\) gives \(\sin(x+y)=1\), so \(y=\cos(x+y)=0\) and \(x=\dfrac\pi2\) or \(-\dfrac{3\pi}2\). Tangents: \(y=-\dfrac12\left(x-\dfrac\pi2\right)\) and \(y=-\dfrac12\left(x+\dfrac{3\pi}2\right)\).

questions.q: Sketch the region bounded by the curves \(y=\sqrt{5-x^2}\) and \(y=|x-1|\) and find its area.
questions.sol: The semicircle meets \(y=|x-1|\) at \((-1,2)\) and \((2,1)\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^2\sqrt{5-x^2}\,dx-\int_{-1}^1(1-x)dx-\int_1^2(x-1)dx=\left(2+\dfrac{5\pi}4\right)-2-\dfrac12\), using \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac2{\sqrt5}+\sin^{-1}\dfrac1{\sqrt5}=\dfrac\pi2\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\sin^3x+\lambda\sin^2x\), \(-\dfrac\pi2<x<\dfrac\pi2\). Find the intervals in which \(\lambda\) should lie in order that \(f(x)\) has exactly one minimum and exactly one maximum.
questions.sol: \(f'=\sin x\cos x(3\sin x+2\lambda)\). Besides \(\sin x=0\) we need a second, different critical point \(\sin x=-\dfrac{2\lambda}3\) inside \((-1,1)\) and non-zero: \(0<|\lambda|<\dfrac32\). Then \(f'\) changes sign at both, giving one maximum and one minimum.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=x^3-x^2+x+1\) and \(g(x)=\begin{cases}\max\{f(t)\mid0\le t\le x\},&0\le x\le1\\3-x,&1<x\le2\end{cases}\) Discuss the continuity and differentiability of the function \(g(x)\) in the interval \((0,2)\).
questions.ans: \(g\) is continuous on \((0,2)\) and differentiable on \((0,2)\) except at \(x=1\)
questions.sol: \(f'=3x^2-2x+1>0\), so \(f\) is increasing and \(g(x)=f(x)\) on \([0,1]\). At \(x=1\): both pieces give \(2\) (continuous), but the slopes are \(f'(1)=2\) and \(-1\).

questions.q: Find the area bounded by the curves \(x^2+y^2=4\), \(x^2=-\sqrt2y\), \(x=y\).
questions.sol: The parabola and the line meet the circle at \((\pm\sqrt2,-\sqrt2)\) and \((\pm\sqrt2,\pm\sqrt2)\). The region bounded by all three lies between the parabola and the line for \(0\le x\le\sqrt2\) and is closed by the arc of the circle from \((\sqrt2,-\sqrt2)\) to \((\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\): \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\sqrt2}\left(x+\dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt2}\right)dx+(\text{segment})=\dfrac53+(\pi-2)\). (The book key prints \(\frac13-\pi\).)

questions.q: Let \(A(p^2,-p)\), \(B(q^2,q)\), \(C(r^2,-r)\) be the vertices of the triangle \(ABC\). A parallelogram \(AFDE\) is drawn with vertices \(D,E\) and \(F\) on the line segments \(BC,CA\) and \(AB\) respectively. Using calculus, show that maximum area of such a parallelogram is \(\dfrac14(p+q)(q+r)(p-r)\).
questions.sol: Let \(AF=x\,AB\) and \(AE=y\,AC\); \(D=A+x\vec{AB}+y\vec{AC}\) lies on \(BC\) iff \(x+y=1\). Area of the parallelogram \(=2xy\Delta=2x(1-x)\Delta\), whose derivative vanishes at \(x=\dfrac12\): maximum \(\dfrac\Delta2\). And \(\Delta=\dfrac12\begin{vmatrix}p^2&-p&1\\q^2&q&1\\r^2&-r&1\end{vmatrix}=\dfrac12(p+q)(q+r)(p-r)\).

questions.q: A \(2\) metre long object is fixed vertically upwards from the mid-point of two locations \(A\) and \(B\), \(8\) metre apart. The speed of the object after \(t\) seconds is given by \(\dfrac{ds}{dt}=(2t+1)\) metres per second. Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the angles subtended by the object at \(A\) and \(B\), respectively after one and two seconds, find the value of \(\cos(\alpha-\beta)\).
questions.sol: \(s=t^2+t\): the object occupies heights \(2\) to \(4\) after \(1\) s and \(6\) to \(8\) after \(2\) s, at horizontal distance \(4\). \(\tan\alpha=\dfrac{1-\frac12}{1+\frac12}=\dfrac13\), \(\tan\beta=\dfrac{2-\frac32}{1+3}=\dfrac18\). \(\tan(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac{5/24}{25/24}=\dfrac15\).

questions.q: Find the point on the curve; \(4x^2+a^2y^2=4a^2\), \(4<a^2<8\) that is farthest from the point \((0,-2)\).
questions.sol: For \((a\cos t,2\sin t)\) with \(s=\sin t\): \(D^2=a^2(1-s^2)+4(s+1)^2=(4-a^2)s^2+8s+a^2+4\). Its vertex is at \(s=\dfrac4{a^2-4}>1\) and the parabola opens downward, so \(D^2\) increases on \([-1,1]\): maximum at \(s=1\).

questions.q: Find the area bounded by the curves \(x^2+y^2=25\), \(4y=|4-x^2|\) and \(x=0\) above the \(x\)-axis.
questions.sol: The curve meets the circle at \((4,3)\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^4\sqrt{25-x^2}\,dx-\int_0^2\dfrac{4-x^2}4dx-\int_2^4\dfrac{x^2-4}4dx=\left(6+\dfrac{25}2\sin^{-1}\dfrac45\right)-\dfrac43-\dfrac83\).

questions.q: Investigate for maxima and minima function \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_1^x\left[2(t-1)(t-2)^3+3(t-1)^2(t-2)^2\right]dt\).
questions.ans: Maximum at \(x=1\), minimum at \(x=\dfrac75\); neither at \(x=2\)

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the curve \(C:y=\tan x\), tangent drawn to \(C\) at \(x=\dfrac\pi4\) and the \(x\)-axis.
questions.sol: The tangent at \(\left(\frac\pi4,1\right)\) has slope \(2\) and meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x=\frac\pi4-\frac12\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan x\,dx-\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac12\cdot1\).

questions.q: Find all maxima and minima of the curve \(y=x(x-1)^2\), \(0\le x\le2\) also determine the area bounded by the curve \(y=x(x-1)^2\), the \(y\)-axis and the line \(y=2\).
questions.ans: Local maximum at \(x=\dfrac13\) \(\left(y=\dfrac4{27}\right)\), local minimum at \(x=1\) \((y=0)\); area \(=\dfrac{10}3\) sq. units
questions.sol: \(y'=(x-1)(3x-1)\). On \([0,2]\) the greatest value is \(y(2)=2\) and the least is \(0\) (at \(x=0,1\)). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^2\left[2-x(x-1)^2\right]dx=4-\dfrac23\).

questions.q: Compute the area of the region bounded by the curves \(y=ex\ln x\) and \(y=\dfrac{\ln x}{ex}\) where \(\ln e=1\).
questions.sol: They meet at \(x=\dfrac1e\) and \(x=1\); between them \(\dfrac{\ln x}{ex}>ex\ln x\). Area \(=\left[\dfrac{(\ln x)^2}{2e}-e\left(\dfrac{x^2\ln x}2-\dfrac{x^2}4\right)\right]_{1/e}^1=\dfrac e4-\dfrac5{4e}\).

questions.q: Sketch the curves and identify the region bounded by \(x=\dfrac12\), \(x=2\), \(y=\ln x\) and \(y=2^x\). Find the area of this region.
questions.sol: \(2^x>\ln x\) throughout. Area \(=\displaystyle\int_{1/2}^2(2^x-\ln x)dx=\left[\dfrac{2^x}{\ln2}-x\ln x+x\right]_{1/2}^2\).

questions.q: A window of perimeter (including the base of the arch) is in the form of a rectangle surrounded by a semi-circle. The semi-circular portion is fitted with coloured glass while the rectangular part is fitted with clear glass. The clear glass transmits three times as much light per square meter as the coloured glass does. What is the ratio for the sides of the rectangle so that the window transmits the maximum light?
questions.sol: Width \(2r\), height \(h\): \(P=2h+4r+\pi r\). Light \(\propto3(2rh)+\dfrac{\pi r^2}2=3r(P-4r-\pi r)+\dfrac{\pi r^2}2\); derivative zero at \(r=\dfrac{3P}{24+5\pi}\), then \(h=\dfrac{(6+\pi)P}{24+5\pi}\). So \(h:2r=(6+\pi):6\).

questions.q: Sketch the region bounded by the curves \(y=x^2\) and \(y=\dfrac2{(1+x^2)}\). Find the area.
questions.sol: They meet at \(x=\pm1\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1\left(\dfrac2{1+x^2}-x^2\right)dx=4\cdot\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac23\).

questions.q: What normal to the curve \(y=x^2\) forms the shortest chord?
questions.sol: The normal at \((t,t^2)\) meets the curve again at \(t'=-t-\dfrac1{2t}\). Chord\(^2=(t-t')^2\left[1+(t+t')^2\right]=4t^2\left(1+\dfrac1{4t^2}\right)^3=\dfrac{(4u+1)^3}{16u^2}\) with \(u=t^2\), least when \(u=\dfrac12\). The normals at \(t=\pm\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) are \(y=\mp\dfrac x{\sqrt2}+1\).

questions.q: Tangent at a point \(P_1\) (other) then \((0,0)\) on the curve \(y=x^3\) meets the curve again at \(P_2\). The tangent at \(P_2\) meets the curve at \(P_3\), and so on. Show that the abscissae of \(P_1,P_2,P_3,\ldots,P_n\) form a G.P. Also find the ratio \(\dfrac{[\text{area}(\Delta P_1P_2P_3)]}{[\text{area}(\Delta P_2P_3P_4)]}\).
questions.sol: The tangent at \((t,t^3)\) is \(y=3t^2x-2t^3\); with the curve: \((x-t)^2(x+2t)=0\), so the next abscissa is \(-2t\): a G.P. with ratio \(-2\). The triangle with abscissae \(t,-2t,4t\) has area proportional to \(t^4\); replacing \(t\) by \(-2t\) multiplies it by \(16\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}-x^3+\dfrac{(b^3-b^2+b-1)}{(b^2+3b+2)},&0\le x<1\\2x-3,&1\le x<3\end{cases}\) Find all possible real values of \(b\) such that \(f(x)\) has the smallest value at \(x=1\).
questions.sol: On \([1,3)\) the least value is \(f(1)=-1\); on \([0,1)\), \(f\) decreases towards \(-1+\dfrac{(b-1)(b^2+1)}{(b+1)(b+2)}\). We need this to be \(\ge-1\): \(\dfrac{b-1}{(b+1)(b+2)}\ge0\).

questions.q: The curve \(y=ax^3+bx^2+cx+5\) touches the \(x\)-axis at \((-2,0)\) and cuts the \(y\)-axis at a point \(Q\) where its gradient is \(3\) find \(a,b,c\).

The circle \(x^2+y^2=1\) cuts the \(x\)-axis at \(P\) and \(Q\). Another circle with centre at \(Q\) and variable radius intersects the first circle at \(R\) above the \(x\)-axis and the line segment \(PQ\) at \(S\). Find the maximum area of \(\Delta QSR\).
questions.sol: With \(Q=(1,0)\), \(R=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\): \(QS=QR=2\sin\dfrac\theta2\) and the height is \(\sin\theta\). Area \(=\sin\dfrac\theta2\sin\theta=2\sin^2u\cos u\) \(\left(u=\dfrac\theta2\right)\), greatest when \(\tan^2u=2\): \(2\cdot\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: In what ratio does the \(x\)-axis divide the area of the region bounded by the parabolas \(y=4x-x^2\) and \(y=x^2-x\)?
questions.sol: They meet at \(x=0,\dfrac52\): total area \(\displaystyle\int_0^{5/2}(5x-2x^2)dx=\dfrac{125}{24}\). Below the axis (where \(x^2-x<0\)): \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(x-x^2)dx=\dfrac16\). Above: \(\dfrac{121}{24}\). Ratio \(\dfrac{121}{24}:\dfrac4{24}\). (The book key prints \(121:24\).)

questions.q: Let a line passing through the fixed point \((h,k)\) cuts the \(x\)-axis at \(P\) and \(y\)-axis at \(Q\). Then find the minimum area of \(\Delta OPQ\).
questions.sol: For the line \(\dfrac xa+\dfrac yb=1\) through \((h,k)\) (with \(h,k>0\)): \(1=\dfrac ha+\dfrac kb\ge2\sqrt{\dfrac{hk}{ab}}\), so \(ab\ge4hk\) and the area \(\dfrac{ab}2\ge2hk\).

questions.q: Let \((1,1)\), \((-1,1)\), \((-1,-1)\), \((1,-1)\) be a vertices of the square and \(S\) the region of all the points insides the square which are nearer to the origin than to any edge. Sketch the region \(S\) and find its area.
questions.sol: Nearer to \(O\) than to the edge \(x=1\): \(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}<1-x\), i.e. \(y^2<1-2x\); similarly for the other edges, so \(S\) is bounded by four parabolas. By symmetry, area \(=8\times\) (part with \(0\le y\le x\)) \(=8\displaystyle\int_0^{\sqrt2-1}\left(\dfrac{1-y^2}2-y\right)dy=8\cdot\dfrac{4\sqrt2-5}6\), where \(y=\sqrt2-1\) is where \(y=x\) meets \(y^2=1-2x\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}xe^{ax},&x\le0\\x+ax^2-x^3,&x>0\end{cases}\) Where \(a\) is a positive constant. Find the interval in which \(f'(x)\) is increasing.
questions.sol: \(x<0\): \(f''=ae^{ax}(2+ax)>0\) for \(x>-\dfrac2a\). \(x>0\): \(f''=2a-6x>0\) for \(x<\dfrac a3\). \(f'\) is continuous at \(0\) (value \(1\) from both sides).

questions.q: A curve \(y=f(x)\) passes through the point \(P(1,1)\). Equation of the normal at \(P(1,1)\) to a curve \(y=f(x)\) is \((x-1)+a(y-1)=0\) and the slope of the tangent at any point on the curve is proportional to the ordinate of the point. Determine the equation of the curve. Also obtain the area bounded by the \(y\)-axis, the curve, and the normal at \(P\).
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=ky\) gives \(y=e^{k(x-1)}\); the tangent at \(P\) has slope \(a\) (normal slope \(-\frac1a\)), so \(k=a\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^1\left[1+\dfrac{1-x}a-e^{a(x-1)}\right]dx=1+\dfrac1{2a}-\dfrac{1-e^{-a}}a\). (The book key prints the area as \(\left(\frac1a+\frac a2\right)-\frac1{2e^a}\).)

questions.q: Determine the points of maxima and minima of the function \(f(x)=\dfrac18\log x-bx+x^2\), \(x>0\). where \(b\ge0\) is a constant.
questions.ans: For \(b>1\): maximum at \(x=\dfrac{b-\sqrt{b^2-1}}4\), minimum at \(x=\dfrac{b+\sqrt{b^2-1}}4\); for \(0\le b\le1\): none
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=\dfrac{16x^2-8bx+1}{8x}\), with roots \(\dfrac{b\pm\sqrt{b^2-1}}4\) when \(b>1\); \(f'\) changes \(+,-,+\). For \(b\le1\), \(f'\ge0\) and \(f\) is increasing.

questions.q: Let \(A_n\) be the area bounded by the curve \(y=(\tan x)^n\) and the lines \(x=0\), \(y=0\) and \(x=\dfrac\pi4\). Prove that for \(n>2\), \(A_n+A_{n-2}=\dfrac1{n-1}\). Hence deduce \(\dfrac1{2n+2}<A_n<\dfrac1{2n-2}\ \forall\ n\).
questions.sol: \(A_n+A_{n-2}=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^{n-2}x\sec^2x\,dx=\dfrac1{n-1}\). As \(0\le\tan x\le1\), \(A_{n+2}<A_n<A_{n-2}\). So \(2A_n<A_n+A_{n-2}=\dfrac1{n-1}\) and \(2A_n>A_n+A_{n+2}=\dfrac1{n+1}\).

questions.q: Let \(S\) be a square of unit area. Consider any quadrilateral which has one vertex on each side of \(S\). If \(a,b,c\) and \(d\) denote the lengths of the sides of the quadrilateral, prove that \(2\le a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2\le4\).
questions.sol: If the vertices divide the sides into parts \(x,1-x\); \(y,1-y\); \(z,1-z\); \(w,1-w\), then by Pythagoras \(a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=\sum\left[t^2+(1-t)^2\right]\) over \(t=x,y,z,w\). For \(0\le t\le1\): \(\dfrac12\le t^2+(1-t)^2\le1\).

questions.q: Let \(a+b=4\), where \(a<2\), and let \(g(x)\) be a differentiable function. If \(dg/dx>0\) for all \(x\), prove that \(\displaystyle\int_0^ag(x)dx+\int_0^bg(x)dx\) increases as \((b-a)\) increases.
questions.sol: Put \(b-a=t\): \(a=2-\dfrac t2\), \(b=2+\dfrac t2\). \(F(t)=\displaystyle\int_0^ag+\int_0^bg\) has \(F'(t)=\dfrac12\left[g(b)-g(a)\right]>0\) since \(b>a\) and \(g\) is increasing.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\text{Maximum}\{x^2,(1-x)^2,2x(1-x)\}\), where \(0\le x\le1\). Determine the area of the region bounded by the curves \(y=f(x)\), \(x\)-axis, \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).
questions.sol: \(f=(1-x)^2\) on \(\left[0,\frac13\right]\), \(2x(1-x)\) on \(\left[\frac13,\frac23\right]\), \(x^2\) on \(\left[\frac23,1\right]\). Area \(=\dfrac{19}{81}+\dfrac{13}{81}+\dfrac{19}{81}\).

questions.q: Find all the possible values of \(b>0\), so that the area of the bounded region enclosed between the parabolas \(y=x-bx^2\) and \(y=\dfrac{x^2}b\) is maximum.
questions.sol: They meet at \(x=0\) and \(x=\dfrac b{1+b^2}\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^{b/(1+b^2)}\left(x-\dfrac{1+b^2}bx^2\right)dx=\dfrac{b^2}{6(1+b^2)^2}\), greatest when \(\dfrac b{1+b^2}\) is greatest: \(b=1\).

questions.q: Let \(O(0,0)\), \(A(2,0)\) and \(B\left(1,\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\right)\) be the vertices of a triangle. Let \(R\) be the region consisting of all those points \(P\) inside \(\Delta OAB\) which satisfy \(d(P,OA)\le\min\{d(P,OB),d(P,AB)\}\), where \(d\) denotes the distance from the point to the corresponding line. Sketch the region \(R\) and find its area.
questions.sol: The points nearer to \(OA\) lie below the bisectors of the angles at \(O\) and \(A\), which meet at the incentre \(I\). \(\angle O=\angle A=30^\circ\), so \(I=(1,\tan15^\circ)=(1,2-\sqrt3)\). \(R\) is the triangle \(OAI\): \(\dfrac12\cdot2\cdot(2-\sqrt3)\).

questions.q: \(A\) and \(B\) are two separate reservoirs of water. Capacity of reservoir \(A\) is double the capacity of reservoir \(B\). Both the reservoirs are filled completely with water, their inlets are closed and then the water is released simultaneously from both the reservoirs. The rate of flow of water out of each reservoir at any instant of time is proportional to the quantity of water in the reservoir at the time. One hour after the water is released, the quantity of water in reservoirs \(A\) is \(1\frac12\) times the quantity of water in reservoir \(B\). After how many hours do both the reservoirs have the same quantity of water?
questions.sol: \(A=2Ve^{-k_1t}\), \(B=Ve^{-k_2t}\), so \(\dfrac AB=2r^t\) with \(r=e^{-(k_1-k_2)}\). At \(t=1\): \(2r=\dfrac32\), \(r=\dfrac34\). \(\dfrac AB=1\) when \(\left(\dfrac34\right)^t=\dfrac12\).

questions.q: A curve \(C\) has to the property that if the tangent drawn at any point \(P\) on \(C\) meets the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\), then \(P\) is the mid-point of \(AB\). The curve passes through the point \((1,1)\). Determine the equation of the curve.
questions.sol: The tangent at \((x,y)\) has intercepts \(x-\dfrac y{y'}\) and \(y-xy'\); the mid-point condition gives \(x-\dfrac y{y'}=2x\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac yx\), so \(xy=c\), and \(c=1\).

For \(P(t,t^2)\): \(Q=\left(\dfrac{t^2}2,t^2\right)\). Area \(OPQ=\displaystyle\int_0^{t^2}\left(\sqrt y-\dfrac y2\right)dy=\dfrac23t^3-\dfrac{t^4}4\) and area \(OPR=\displaystyle\int_0^t\left(x^2-f(x)\right)dx\). Equating and differentiating: \(2t^2-t^3=t^2-f(t)\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\) be a continuous function given by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}2x,&|x|\le1\\x^2+ax+b,&|x|>1\end{cases}\) Find the area of the region in the third quadrant bounded by the curves \(x=-2y^2\) and \(y=f(x)\) lying on the left of the line \(8x+1=0\).
questions.sol: Continuity at \(\pm1\) gives \(a=2\), \(b=-1\). The lower branch \(y=-\sqrt{-x/2}\) meets \(y=2x\) at \(x=-\dfrac18\) and \(y=x^2+2x-1\) at \(x=-2\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{-1}\left[-\sqrt{\dfrac{-x}2}-(x^2+2x-1)\right]dx+\int_{-1}^{-1/8}\left[-\sqrt{\dfrac{-x}2}-2x\right]dx=-\dfrac{21}{16}+\dfrac53+\dfrac{63}{64}\). (The book key prints \(\frac{761}{192}\).)

questions.q: Let \(b\ne0\) and for \(j=0,1,2,\ldots,n\). Let \(S_j\) be the area of the region bounded by \(y\)-axis and the curve \(xe^{ay}=\sin by\), \(\dfrac{j\pi}b\le y\le\dfrac{(j+1)\pi}b\) show that so, \(S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_n\) are in geometric progression. Also, find their sum for \(a=-1\), and \(b=\pi\).
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int e^{-ay}\sin by\,dy=\dfrac{e^{-ay}(-a\sin by-b\cos by)}{a^2+b^2}\), so \(S_j=\dfrac{|b|}{a^2+b^2}e^{-aj\pi/b}\left(1+e^{-a\pi/b}\right)\): a G.P. with ratio \(e^{-a\pi/b}\). For \(a=-1\), \(b=\pi\): \(S_j=\dfrac{\pi(1+e)}{1+\pi^2}e^j\), summed over \(j=0,\ldots,n\).

questions.q: Let \(-1\le p\le1\). Show that the equation \(4x^3-3x-p=0\) has a unique root in the interval \(\left[\dfrac12,1\right]\) and identify it.
questions.sol: \(f(x)=4x^3-3x-p\): \(f\left(\frac12\right)=-1-p\le0\), \(f(1)=1-p\ge0\) and \(f'=3(4x^2-1)>0\) on \(\left(\frac12,1\right]\): exactly one root. With \(x=\cos\theta\), \(\theta\in\left[0,\frac\pi3\right]\): \(\cos3\theta=p\).

questions.q:
A hemispherical tank of radius \(2\) metres is initially full of water and has an outlet of \(12\) cm\(^2\) cross-sectional area at the bottom. The outlet is opened at same instant. The flow through the outlet is according to the law \(v(t)=0\cdot6\sqrt{2gh(t)}\), where \(v(t)\) and \(h(t)\) are respectively the velocity of the flow through the outlet and the height of water level above the outlet at time \(t\), and \(g\) is the acceleration due to gravity. Find the time it takes to empty the tank.
(Hint : For a differential equation by relating the decrease of water level to the outflow).
questions.sol: In cm: when the depth is \(h\) the surface has radius\(^2=400h-h^2\), so \(\pi(400h-h^2)dh=-12(0.6)\sqrt{2gh}\,dt\). \(T=\dfrac\pi{7.2\sqrt{2g}}\displaystyle\int_0^{200}\left(400h^{1/2}-h^{3/2}\right)dh=\dfrac\pi{7.2\sqrt{2g}}\cdot200^{3/2}\left(\dfrac{800}3-80\right)\).

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the curves \(y=x^2\), \(y=|2-x^2|\) and \(y=2\), which lies to the right of the line \(x=1\).
questions.sol: Area \(=\displaystyle\int_1^{\sqrt2}\left[x^2-(2-x^2)\right]dx+\int_{\sqrt2}^2\left[2-(x^2-2)\right]dx=\left(\dfrac43-\dfrac{2\sqrt2}3\right)+\left(\dfrac{16}3-\dfrac{10\sqrt2}3\right)\).

questions.q: If the function \(f:[0,4]\to R\) is differentiable then show that for \(a,b\in(0,4)\), \((f(4))^2-(f(0))^2=8f'(a)f(b)\).
questions.sol: Mean value theorem: \(f(4)-f(0)=4f'(a)\). Intermediate value theorem: \(\dfrac{f(4)+f(0)}2=f(b)\) for some \(b\) (it lies between \(f(0)\) and \(f(4)\)). Multiply the two.

questions.q: If \(p(x)=51x^{101}-2323x^{100}-45x+1035\), using Rolle's Theorem prove that atleast one root lies between \((45^{1/100},46)\).
Find the area bounded by the curves \(x^2=y\), \(x^2=-y\) and \(y^2=4x-3\).
questions.sol: \(y^2=4x-3\) touches \(y=\pm x^2\) at \((1,\pm1)\). By symmetry, area \(=2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^1x^2dx-\int_{3/4}^1\sqrt{4x-3}\,dx\right]=2\left[\dfrac13-\dfrac16\right]\).

questions.q: \(f(x)\) is a differentiable function and \(g(x)\) is a double differentiable function such that \(|f(x)|\le1\) and \(f'(x)=g(x)\). If \(f^2(0)+g^2(0)=9\). Prove that there exists some \(c\in(-3,3)\) such that \(g(c)\cdot g''(c)<0\)
questions.sol: By the mean value theorem there are \(c_1\in(0,3)\), \(c_2\in(-3,0)\) with \(|g(c_i)|=|f'(c_i)|\le\dfrac23\). For \(h=f^2+g^2\): \(h(c_i)\le1+\dfrac49<9=h(0)\), so \(h\) has a maximum at some \(c\in(c_2,c_1)\) with \(h(c)\ge9\); hence \(g(c)^2\ge8\). \(h'=2g(f+g')=0\) gives \(g'(c)=-f(c)\), and \(h''(c)=2g(c)\left(g(c)+g''(c)\right)\le0\) gives \(g(c)g''(c)\le-g(c)^2<0\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)\) is a cubic polynomial having maxima at \(x=-1\) and \(f'(x)\) has minima at \(x=1\), also \(f(-1)=10\), \(f(1)=-6\). Find the cubic polynomial and also find the distance between the points, which are maxima or minima.
questions.sol: \(f'=k(x+1)(x-m)\) with \(f''(1)=0\) gives \(m=3\): \(f=k\left(\dfrac{x^3}3-x^2-3x\right)+c\). The two values give \(k=3\), \(c=5\). Maximum \((-1,10)\), minimum \((3,-22)\): distance \(\sqrt{16+1024}\).

questions.q: Given \(\begin{bmatrix}4a^2&4a&1\\4b^2&4b&1\\4c^2&4c&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}f(-1)\\f(1)\\f(2)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3a^2+3a\\3b^2+3b\\3c^2+3c\end{bmatrix}\) and \(f(x)\) is a quadratic polynomial. \(V\) is a point of maxima of \(f(x)\) and '\(A\)' is the point where \(f(x)\) cuts the \(x\)-axis. '\(B\)' is a point such that \(AB\) subtends a right angle at \(V\)? Find area between the chord \(AB\) and \(f(x)\).
questions.sol: \((4f(-1)-3)x^2+(4f(1)-3)x+f(2)=0\) has three roots \(a,b,c\), so it is an identity: \(f(-1)=f(1)=\dfrac34\), \(f(2)=0\), giving \(f=1-\dfrac{x^2}4\). \(V=(0,1)\), \(A=(-2,0)\); \(B=\left(t,1-\dfrac{t^2}4\right)\) with \(\vec{VA}\cdot\vec{VB}=-2t+\dfrac{t^2}4=0\), \(t=8\). Area between a parabola and a chord: \(\dfrac{|a|(x_2-x_1)^3}6=\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac{1000}6\).

questions.q: For a twice differentiable function \(f(x)\), \(g(x)\) is defined as \(g(x)=(f'(x)^2+f''(x))f(x)\) on \([a,e]\). If for \(a<b<c<d<e\), \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=2\), \(f(c)=-1\), \(f(d)=2\), \(f(e)=0\) then find the minimum number of zeros of \(g(x)\).
questions.sol: \(g=\left(f'\right)^2+ff''=(ff')'\). \(f\) has at least \(4\) zeros (\(a\), one in \((b,c)\), one in \((c,d)\), \(e\)) and so \(f'\) has at least \(3\) zeros between them. \(ff'\) has at least \(7\) zeros, hence its derivative \(g\) has at least \(6\).

questions.q: If \(x-r\) is a factor of the polynomial \(f(x)=a_nx^n+\ldots+a_0\), repeated \(m\) times \((1<m\le n)\), then \(r\) is a root of \(f'(x)=0\) repeated \(m\) times.
questions.sol: \(f=(x-r)^mg(x)\) with \(g(r)\ne0\) gives \(f'=(x-r)^{m-1}\left[mg+(x-r)g'\right]\): \(r\) is repeated only \(m-1\) times.

questions.q: For \(0<a<x\), the minimum value of the function \(\log_ax+\log_xa\) is \(2\).
questions.sol: With \(t=\log_ax\) the function is \(t+\dfrac1t\), which equals \(2\) only at \(x=a\) (excluded). If \(a<1\) it can even be negative (e.g. \(x>1\) gives \(t<0\)).

Consider the functions \(f,g:R\to R\) defined by \(f(x)=x^2+\dfrac5{12}\) and \(g(x)=\begin{cases}2\left(1-\dfrac{4|x|}3\right),&|x|\le\dfrac34,\\0,&|x|>\dfrac34\end{cases}\)
if \(\alpha\) is the area of the region \(\left\{(x,y)\in R\times R:|x|\le\dfrac34,\ 0\le y\le\min\{f(x),g(x)\}\right\}\), then the value of \(9\alpha\) is ______.
questions.sol: For \(x\ge0\), \(f=g\) at \(x=\dfrac12\) (value \(\dfrac23\)). \(\alpha=2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}\left(x^2+\dfrac5{12}\right)dx+\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac23\right]=2\left[\dfrac14+\dfrac1{12}\right]=\dfrac23\).

Let \(n\ge2\) be a natural number and \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) be the function defined by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}n(1-2nx)&\text{if }0\le x\le\dfrac1{2n}\\2n(2nx-1)&\text{if }\dfrac1{2n}\le x\le\dfrac3{4n}\\4n(1-nx)&\text{if }\dfrac3{4n}\le x\le\dfrac1n\\\dfrac n{n-1}(nx-1)&\text{if }\dfrac1n\le x\le1\end{cases}\)
If \(n\) is such that the area of the region bounded by the curves \(x=0\), \(x=1\), \(y=0\) and \(y=f(x)\) is \(4\), then the maximum value of the function \(f\) is
questions.sol: The graph is made of triangles of height \(n\) on bases \(\dfrac1{2n},\dfrac1{2n},1-\dfrac1n\): area \(\dfrac14+\dfrac14+\dfrac{n-1}2=\dfrac n2=4\), so \(n=8\), and the maximum of \(f\) is \(n\).

questions.q: For \(x\in\mathbb R\), let \(\tan^{-1}(x)\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then the minimum value of the function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^{x\tan^{-1}x}\dfrac{e^{(t-\cos t)}}{1+t^{2023}}dt\) is
questions.sol: \(x\tan^{-1}x\ge0\) for all \(x\) and the integrand is positive for \(t\ge0\), so \(f\ge0\) with \(f(0)=0\).

Let the function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{\sin x}{e^{\pi x}}\dfrac{(x^{2023}+2024x+2025)}{(x^2-x+3)}+\dfrac2{e^{\pi x}}\dfrac{(x^{2023}+2024x+2025)}{(x^2-x+3)}\)
Then the number of solutions of \(f(x)=0\) in \(\mathbb R\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(f=\dfrac{(\sin x+2)(x^{2023}+2024x+2025)}{e^{\pi x}(x^2-x+3)}\) and \(\sin x+2>0\). \(x^{2023}+2024x+2025\) is strictly increasing, with its only root at \(x=-1\).
